New Relic announced that application log collection would be enabled by default starting 5/3. Its own FAQ admitted the extra logs would be ingested at the standard rate, which commenters read as an automatic, opt-out bill increase.
Workaround: setting the env vars NEW_RELIC_APPLICATION_LOGGING_ENABLED=false and NEW_RELIC_APPLICATION_LOGGING_FORWARDING_ENABLED=false disables the new default log collection.

Free-account user: automatic log collection can be turned off in the Data Management Hub under 'log settings'. Another user said you can ask New Relic to switch it off for all of your company's accounts before go-live.

New Relic's logging agent had a bug that lost a good portion of our logs for months. Support was extremely lethargic diagnosing it and not apologetic once they confirmed the bug. We moved logging to Datadog and it's been generally better.
Reminds me of when they intentionally enabled JFR on every single Java process. It roughly sextupled our ingest (and associated costs) until we got it shut back off.

When they changed billing to per-user, our bill went up 20x for no additional value. I still haven't found a better APM product that ticks all the boxes. But APM hasn't seen a single new feature in the 5 years I've used it.
New Relic is one of the most expensive items in our budget. Last year I had to tell a producer that the SaaS monitoring our servers cost more than the servers themselves.

Small environment (~20 VMs) quickly exceeded the 100GB free tier with just APM metrics. It was impossible to figure out how to filter out irrelevant metrics, and support/community weren't helpful. Log ingest for one VM was several GB/day, 99% irrelevant, and hard to filter.

I've used NR for close to 15 years and have been disappointed by the last ~5. They removed development mode, changed the price model, and the new UI is buggy and keeps changing for the worse, which hurts when things are on fire. But it's still very useful, and finding an alternative is a time investment I haven't made yet.
End user at a mid/large company: all I do in NR is run queries by key name and get a nice graph. It doesn't feel like it's doing anything that fancy beyond the graph.

I love NewRelic, but their pricing baffled me. Adding it to QA, UAT and Staging got us billed as if we had 3x the production environments, despite those getting a tiny fraction of the traffic. Redundant regions/AZs were also billed per instance, making it crazy expensive.

Our customers don't care much about open-source agents, but they do care where the server is. There's a huge underserved market for on-prem APM, and the on-prem options you can buy aren't nearly as good as New Relic.

Choosing between Datadog and New Relic at a unicorn startup, Datadog's open-source client libraries were a major advantage. They let us extend them to support our very old Django version and homegrown SOA framework.

We're stuck with New Relic because its APM metrics for .NET, Java and JavaScript are decent and it's nice having everything in one dashboard. But the new UI is pretty difficult to use and way too bright. We're exploring more affordable competitors.

Used New Relic APM and Server Monitoring via BizSpark. The product was good, but multi-server pricing was starkly high for a small company and it felt enterprise-focused. We switched to Prometheus + Grafana + Exceptional, set it up in a week, and never looked back.

I've long preferred New Relic; important info was easy to find, and other APMs seemed inaccurate or harder to navigate. But we had constant metric-name explosions: high-traffic unique URLs got their own metric names until metric creation was locked, despite explicit naming via the SDK.
I'm paying a pretty penny to monitor production, yet New Relic charges for development environments while other vendors give development licenses for free.

I used New Relic for the first time at my current job. The service it provides our team is invaluable, but the UI is slow and very confusing. I can never remember which button or menu gets me where I need to go, and the slow loading makes it worse.
Currently using NR, but it's slow, expensive, and the in-cluster collection services are frustratingly fragile.

Our devs use both Azure Application Insights and New Relic. New Relic appears useful but is too slow in practice, so devs avoid it day-to-day. Outside the US, the cloud-hosted version is especially slow due to trans-oceanic latency, whereas App Insights can be deployed in-region and feels faster.

Users objected to New Relic turning on production log collection by default after an upgrade. Per the company's FAQ, the extra ingested data is billed at the standard ingest rate, which commenters called an automatic opt-out bill increase.
Workaround: set the env vars NEW_RELIC_APPLICATION_LOGGING_ENABLED=false and NEW_RELIC_APPLICATION_LOGGING_FORWARDING_ENABLED=false to disable the new default log collection.
